text: Colibacillosis (E. coli infection) is the most common infectious disease of farmed poultry. E. coli is a normal gut inhabitant, but stress or another infection (e.g. Mycoplasma) can let it cause septicemia; house dust also carries a lot of E. coli. In chicks, infection often happens via the egg, when feces contaminate the shell surface and E. coli penetrates through it. Symptoms: high chick mortality, high embryonic mortality, respiratory distress, white-to-yellowish-green diarrhea, and cellulitis (infection under the skin). Necropsy findings: fibrinous material on the heart, liver, and air sacs; an abnormal, distended, cloudy, foul-smelling yolk sac in chicks — unlike Salmonella, there is no grey necrotic spot on the liver. Treatment: resistance to many antibiotics is common; Chlortetracycline combined with Colistin, or Flumequine combined with Amoxicillin, are recommended.
